title: Agent with tool-calling, not prompt engineering or RAG
reason: The app needs to reliably change real data — your intake answers, plan status, which step you're on — and a prompt by itself can't guarantee that happens correctly every time. It also needs to search the live web for current market info when generating ideas, not just pull from a fixed set of pre-loaded documents (which is what a "RAG" search over a static corpus would give it).
tradeoff: One AI model handles the whole conversation — intake, ideas, your plan, check-ins — end to end, instead of splitting the work across several coordinating AI agents. Simpler to build and reason about, at the cost of not having a specialist agent dedicated to any one task.

title: Three-tier memory split
reason: Anything that has to be correct — your current step, whether your plan is active, your timeline — is stored in the main database and re-read fresh every time it's needed, never relied on from the chat's own internal memory. That internal memory is used only to keep the conversation flowing naturally; it's never treated as the source of truth for what's actually true about your plan.
tradeoff: A little more engineering work for every feature (each one fetches fresh data rather than reusing what's already in memory) — in exchange, the app can never act on outdated or half-remembered information.

title: Tool boundary: LLM-backed vs. plain-code vs. MCP
reason: Anything that changes your actual saved data (intake answers, plan steps, check-ins) is handled by fixed, predictable code — never directly by the AI model. The AI only generates content (ideas, plan drafts); a separate, non-AI step is what actually saves it, so an unpredictable AI response can never corrupt your data.
tradeoff: The idea- and plan-generating tools do save their own output directly, rather than handing it to a separate tool to save — but that saving step itself is still plain, predictable code, not the AI, so the safety guarantee above still holds.

title: activate_plan human-in-the-loop gate
reason: Before a plan can go live, the app always pauses and waits for you to explicitly confirm it — this step can't be skipped. The database also enforces that you can only have one active plan at a time.
tradeoff: One extra click before a plan starts, every time — you always have to approve or reject it first. In exchange, a plan can never silently go live without your say-so.

title: Moderation hook placement
reason: A content-safety check runs at three fixed points in every conversation — right before your message reaches the AI, around every web search, and right after the AI replies — rather than being added inconsistently in different places. Attempts to manipulate the AI get rejected outright; personal information (like an email address) is automatically blanked out rather than rejecting your whole message; and any unsafe reply is swapped out before you ever see it.
tradeoff: A reused (cached) web-search result is always one that's already passed this safety check, so reusing it never skips moderation — the cost is that every new search result gets checked once up front, even the ones that turn out to be perfectly safe.

title: Guilt/streak-language guardrail
reason: A separate, more targeted check looks specifically for guilt-tripping or shaming language (like calling out a "broken streak") right after the AI replies. It needed its own dedicated check because the general safety check above has no category that covers this.
tradeoff: If a reply gets flagged, the AI gets up to 2 tries to rephrase it without the guilt-tripping language; if it still can't, the app falls back to a plain, neutral message instead of trying forever. That guarantees you always get a reply — just not always a perfectly polished one.
